texts: Here's what you need to know about the noteworthy features of Shadow element.
Implement shadows to add depth and dimension to your elements, enhancing the overall visual hierarchy of your user interface.
Explore a wide array of shadow styles, from standard shadows to those meticulously tailored for specific UI components.
Shadows are tailored to specific components such as buttons, toggles, checkboxes, and more, enhancing their individual characteristics.

Shadows play a critical role in design, creating depth and visual hierarchy within your interface. By casting shadows, elements stand out and gain a sense of realism, engaging users and providing an intuitive experience. Shadows are especially effective in emphasizing interactive elements like buttons, modals, and cards, guiding users' attention and interactions.

Knowing when and how to apply shadows is essential. Thoughtful use of shadows enhances the overall aesthetics, adding a touch of realism while maintaining a clean and engaging design. By carefully considering shadow placement, size, and intensity, you can achieve a balanced and effective visual composition that enhances user experience.
Tip: It's important to keep shadows fairly subtle; overly strong shadows can be distracting and work against your design.

Begin by adding an Ellipse shape onto a white background frame – this will allow you to perceive shadows more distinctly.

Once you click on the Ellipse, navigate to the "Effects" section in the right panel. Hovering over this section reveals the "Style" icon. Clicking on it grants you access to the shadow styles. Picking a shadow will be applied to the selected frame, shape, or other elements.
Tip: You can see the applied shadow effects in the right panel. To remove shadows, simply click on the “-” icon."

When you add a shadow effect into an element, you can click on the “Style” icon and then the add icon to “Create a New Style”. Once you add a name to your style, you are ready to click to the button and create style.

When you apply a shadow effect to an element, click on the "Style" icon and then the add icon to "Create a New Style". Assign a relevant name to your style, then proceed to create it with a simple click of the button.
Tip: Use this format to group your effect styles: (group-name) / (style-name)

You can also access the shadow styles by navigating to the "Effect Styles" section on the right panel. Clicking on the settings icon of a specific shadow style allows you to delve into the finer details and properties associated with it. This way, you can fine-tune your shadow effects to perfectly match your design requirements.
In certain cases, you might see multiple shadows within a shadow style. The presence of multiple shadows is aimed at achieving the desired and optimal shadow effect.

If you wish to customize these individual shadows, you can do so by clicking on the icons. This will grant you the ability to adjust various properties, including position, color, opacity, and the amount of blur and spread.
Consistency in design and adherence to the design system's principles are ensured through carefully crafted radius values.
Here's what you need to know about the noteworthy features of Corner Radius element.

The choice of radius values can play a crucial role in defining a brand's visual identity. Consistently using specific radius values across various design elements can help reinforce brand recognition and establish a distinct visual style that sets the brand apart from competitors.

Rounded corners can help optimize space within a design by reducing visual clutter and creating a smoother flow between elements. This can be particularly useful in interfaces where space is limited or where a clean and minimalist aesthetic is desired.

Rounded corners can improve accessibility by reducing the risk of sharp edges that may cause discomfort or confusion for users, especially those with visual or cognitive impairments. Carefully chosen radius values contribute to a more inclusive design.
Consistency in design and adherence to the design system's principles are ensured through carefully crafted radius values.
Here's what you need to know about the noteworthy features of Motion & Animation element.
Ensure seamless transitions between states to maintain a coherent user experience. Use motion to establish visual continuity and reinforce the connection between related elements.

Maintain consistency in motion across your designs to establish familiarity and build trust with our users. Consistent motion patterns facilitate intuitive navigation and streamline user interactions.
Prioritize performance and accessibility in motion. Ensure that animations enhance rather than hinder usability, and consider the impact on users with disabilities or slower devices.

guidelineTexts: Here's what you need to know about the noteworthy features of Grid System element.

Our Grid System enforces precise alignment and spacing rules for elements, eliminating the guesswork and manual adjustments. This results in a harmonious visual structure that enhances the overall aesthetics and readability.

We've designed four grid layouts that dynamically adjust to different navigation sidebar and topbar placements, ensuring your dashboards remain consistent and organized, no matter the design approach.
The 12-column structure provides flexibility when adding widgets to your dashboard. You can easily position three widgets, each spanning three, four, or more columns, or explore other possibilities.
Designed for situations where you have an expanded sidebar, offering 272px width for your main content.
Designed for situations where you have a collapsed sidebar, providing a narrower 80px width for your content area.
Designed for situations where you have both a collapsed sidebar and a submenu, offering 80px for the sidebar and 264px for the submenu content.
Designed for situations when you use a topbar instead of a sidebar. It creates safe areas of 80px on both sides for your content.

Before you dive into locating and applying a grid, it's recommended to begin by creating a frame with dimensions of 1440x900 pixels. The choice of 1440 pixels is rooted in its optimal suitability for web design.

Once you click on the frame, you'll notice the "Layout Grid" option awaiting your attention on the right-hand panel. By hovering over this option and spotting the "Style" icon, simply click on it to gain access to the grids we have prepared for your convenience. Clicking on any of these grids will apply it to your frame, enabling you to craft designs with consistency.
Tip: When you apply a grid to a frame, using the keyboard shortcut “Shift + G” enables you to show/hide layout grids.

When you explore the settings of one of our layout grids, you'll find a variety of grids, each with different characteristics that work together to create a complete layout.

Clicking on these settings icons of the inner grids gives you more details about that particular grid. This information helps you better understand how the grid is structured and assists you in making design decisions.
“Grid 4px” is designed to align with 4-pixel increments, which guarantees consistent spacing for all your design elements. It’s currently hidden, you can unhide it as you wish.
“1 column (272px)” grid is specifically crafted to house navigation sidebar content, which provides a generous 272px width for a single column.

“12 columns (70px)” grid is designed for widget content, which assigns 70px to each of its 12 columns, maintaining a 24px gap between them. It also features a 304px offset in total, including both the 272px width of "1 Column (272px)" and a 32px safe area.

When applying grids to your frame, you'll unlock two key functionalities that enhance your design process. The first is to use arranged sizes to guide your design decisions, ensuring consistency and visual harmony. The second empowers you with alignment precision by leveraging grid lines to automatically snap your elements. To use this snapping feature, ensure that the "Snap to pixel grid" feature is enabled within Figma's Preferences.

For optimal grid-based design, consider adjusting your "Nudge Amount." This setting dictates the distance your elements move when using your keyboard's arrow keys. A small nudge involves moving your item based on the set nudge amount, while a big nudge occurs when you hold the "Shift" key and adjust with a larger increment.

Given our system's 4-pixel increments, we recommend setting your small nudge to 1 pixel and your big nudge to 8 pixels. You can find this feature within Figma's Preferences again. These values align seamlessly with our grid's structure, enabling precise alignment and effortless adjustments as you craft your designs.
